article:
The first thing people in many countries may notice as they walk into large supermarkets is that getting into the store is much easier than getting out. 16______ This means that customers end up having to walk through half of the store to find a way out, seeing more things they want to buy on the way.
Once they're inside, the first products many shoppers often see are fruit and vegetables. 17______ If that were the case, fruit and vegetables, many of which are easily damaged, could be put on top of the other shopping. But having them near the entrance can make customers feel that everything in the store is fresh and healthy, encouraging them to buy more.
What customers might also notice as they enter is the smell of freshly baked bread. This attracts many people towards the bakery to buy some. 18______ Putting it in this location makes sure that shoppers walk past as many other products as possible to reach their delicious bread.
Research shows that if music is played in supermarkets, customers slow down and spend more time shopping. 19______ And supermarkets know, of course, that this also means they'll buy more products.
In some countries, when customers finally arrive at the queue for the checkouts, they find themselves face - to - face with shelves full of small, inexpensive products like chocolate and sweets. 20______ So they're often bought by tired parents to keep their bored sons or daughters entertained as they pack their shopping. Products placed next to checkouts sell up to eight times faster than in other parts of a store.

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: In one study, they actually stayed 34% longer than if there was none.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: As a result, shoppers pass the cheaper products more quickly.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: That's why expensive products are placed at the same height as people's eyes.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: In fact, it would be more convenient for customers to reach this section later.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: Many of these are designed to attract children.

sentences.label: F
sentences.text: That's because they often have entry doors that can't be used as exits.

sentences.label: G
sentences.text: This would encourage customers and their children to leave the store too quickly.

sentences.label: H
sentences.text: However, it's often right at the back of the store.

explanations.16: 超市入口易进难出，F选项“That's because they often have entry doors that can't be used as exits.”（因入口不能作出口）解释原因，与“walk through half of the store to find a way out”逻辑衔接。
explanations.17: 果蔬放门口，D选项“In fact, it would be more convenient for customers to reach this section later.”（稍后买更方便）提出反常识观点，与“make customers feel everything is fresh”形成对比。
explanations.18: 面包香味吸引顾客，H选项“However, it's often right at the back of the store.”（但面包在店后方）说明位置设计，与“walk past as many products as possible”呼应。
explanations.19: 音乐让顾客放慢脚步，A选项“In one study, they actually stayed 34% longer than if there was none.”（研究显示停留时间长34%）用数据支撑，与“spend more time shopping”对应。
explanations.20: 收银台旁放小商品，E选项“Many of these are designed to attract children.”（吸引孩子）解释目标群体，与“tired parents to keep their bored sons or daughters entertained”衔接。
